title: TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control
motivation: Make latent world-model control robust and scalable across many continuous-control tasks without task-specific tuning.
state_action: Vector or image observation encoded to a latent state; continuous action is concatenated into latent dynamics and reward prediction.
prediction_targets: Next latent state, reward, termination, policy prior, and an ensemble of Q estimates.
training_horizon: Multi-step latent consistency, reward, termination, and value losses with rho-based temporal weighting.
planning: MPPI/CEM-like receding-horizon latent planning; mixes policy-prior trajectories with sampled trajectories and adds terminal Q.
uncertainty_safety: Multiple Q heads use clipped/min or average aggregation, but this is value conservatism rather than a calibrated dynamics ensemble or a traffic safety fallback.
protocol_baselines: 104 continuous-control tasks across four domains; compares model-based and model-free methods including TD-MPC, DreamerV3, and SAC.
result_summary: The paper reports strong fixed-hyperparameter performance and scaling to a 317M-parameter multi-task agent; these results do not establish discrete TSC performance.
limitation: The action space and planner are continuous; direct application to heterogeneous discrete phase masks and coupled intersection actions is not established.
traffic_inspiration: Reuse the loss decomposition and terminal-value pattern, not the continuous MPPI action parameterization.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract, Sec. 3-4 and Fig. 1; code tdmpc2/common/world_model.py:26-30,114-215 and tdmpc2/tdmpc2.py:123-203,268-303

title: Mastering Diverse Control Tasks through World Models (DreamerV3)
motivation: Build one robust world-model RL algorithm that works across diverse tasks with fixed hyperparameters.
state_action: Images or vector observations are encoded into recurrent discrete latent states conditioned on previous actions.
prediction_targets: Observation reconstruction, reward, continuation, latent dynamics; separate actor and distributional critic learn on imagined states.
training_horizon: Sequence world-model training and imagined actor-critic rollouts with value bootstrapping.
planning: A learned actor selects actions at execution; the model supplies imagined trajectories for actor and critic training rather than online candidate MPC.
uncertainty_safety: Robust normalization, free bits, KL balancing, and distributional value prediction; no explicit ensemble disagreement or MaxPressure-style fallback.
protocol_baselines: More than 150 tasks across eight domains with fixed hyperparameters; the paper includes ablations of model signals and robustness techniques.
result_summary: The article reports broad fixed-configuration performance and shows that several robustness components matter on subsets of tasks.
limitation: The full actor-critic system is a large architectural change and provides no direct evidence for CityFlow structured states or discrete joint phase planning.
traffic_inspiration: Reward/continuation/value heads and sequence training support the multi-step hypothesis; wholesale migration is out of scope.
evidence_pointer: article Fig. 1, Learning algorithm, World model learning, Critic learning, Evaluation and Fig. 6; code dreamerv3/agent.py:156-244,382-482

title: Trajectory World Models for Heterogeneous Environments
motivation: Pretrain one low-dimensional world model despite different sensor and actuator schemas across environments.
state_action: Tokenized trajectory variables with observation/action indicators, padding masks, and variable masks.
prediction_targets: Distributional next observation and reward; environment termination is supplied by task-specific termination functions.
training_horizon: Autoregressive trajectory training over context windows; pretraining masks variables to support heterogeneous schemas.
planning: Online MPC evaluates proposed action sequences with the learned trajectory model; policy proposals can seed candidates.
uncertainty_safety: Distribution entropy, confidence, prediction standard deviation, or kNN distance can penalize reward; these are not all calibrated epistemic uncertainty.
protocol_baselines: UniTraj contains over one million trajectories from 80 environments; evaluation covers transition prediction, off-policy evaluation, and online MPC.
result_summary: The official ICML page reports gains in all three evaluation uses, but no traffic-signal environment is included.
limitation: No repository license is declared and the provided MPC assumes continuous actions and task-specific termination logic.
traffic_inspiration: Intersection/roadnet masks can play the role of heterogeneous variable indicators; pretraining should be tested only after within-city dynamics is reliable.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract and Sec. 3-5; code dynamics/trajworld_dynamics.py:375-515 and mpc/mpc.py:54-126,201-231

title: Do Transformer World Models Give Better Policy Gradients?
motivation: Long-horizon policy gradients through common world models can follow circuitous and hard-to-optimize computational paths.
state_action: Action-conditioned transformer formulations provide direct paths from action sequences to future outcomes.
prediction_targets: Future outcomes/rewards used for differentiable policy optimization.
training_horizon: Long-horizon action-conditioned modeling designed around gradient-path structure.
planning: Differentiable policy-gradient optimization through the action-conditioned model, not discrete candidate enumeration.
uncertainty_safety: No central calibrated uncertainty or fallback mechanism in the core claim.
protocol_baselines: Realistic long-horizon control tasks compare transformer world-model variants and policy optimization landscapes.
result_summary: The paper reports that its action-conditioned models produce easier optimization landscapes and better policies than competitive baselines.
limitation: Its core benefit concerns backpropagated policy gradients; our current planner ranks discrete candidates without differentiating through actions.
traffic_inspiration: The useful translation is explicit joint-action-to-future conditioning, not the policy-gradient claim itself.
evidence_pointer: official PMLR page lines 8-25; paper Sec. 3-5

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Handful of Trials using Probabilistic Dynamics Models
motivation: Improve model-based RL sample efficiency without giving up asymptotic control performance.
state_action: Continuous states and actions feed probabilistic neural dynamics models.
prediction_targets: A Gaussian distribution over state changes; bootstrapped ensemble members represent distinct learned dynamics.
training_horizon: One-step probabilistic models are propagated by trajectory sampling through the planning horizon.
planning: Cross-entropy method searches action sequences and executes the first action in MPC fashion.
uncertainty_safety: Aleatoric uncertainty comes from predictive distributions and epistemic uncertainty from ensemble disagreement.
protocol_baselines: Four continuous-control benchmarks against model-based and model-free baselines; the paper emphasizes interaction count.
result_summary: The official abstract reports matching model-free asymptotic performance on several tasks with many fewer samples.
limitation: Continuous CEM and Gaussian state dynamics do not map directly to masked discrete phases, and disagreement must be calibrated before acting as a safety signal.
traffic_inspiration: Train independently bootstrapped traffic dynamics heads and test whether disagreement predicts candidate ranking error.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract, Sec. 4 and Algorithm 1; official NeurIPS reviews describe ensemble plus CEM trajectory sampling

title: When to Trust Your Model: Model-Based Policy Optimization
motivation: Balance cheap model-generated data against bias that grows with model rollout length.
state_action: Continuous states/actions with learned probabilistic dynamics; real replay states seed imagined rollouts.
prediction_targets: One-step next-state/reward dynamics used to generate short synthetic branches.
training_horizon: Short model rollouts branch from real data; rollout horizon is a controlled source of bias.
planning: Uses model data to train a policy rather than performing online candidate MPC.
uncertainty_safety: The main safeguard is deliberately short model use tied to empirical model generalization, not a deployment fallback.
protocol_baselines: Continuous-control evaluation compares sample efficiency and asymptotic performance against prior MBRL and model-free methods.
result_summary: The official abstract reports that short branched rollouts retain gains while avoiding failure at long horizons.
limitation: It does not show that minimizing one-step MSE improves counterfactual action ranking in discrete traffic control.
traffic_inspiration: Treat rollout horizon as an ablation and prefer real-state-rooted counterfactual evaluation over unrestricted synthetic trajectories.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract, Sec. 3-5 and Algorithm 1

title: MOPO: Model-based Offline Policy Optimization
motivation: Prevent an offline policy from exploiting learned dynamics outside the logged data distribution.
state_action: Offline continuous-control transitions train an ensemble probabilistic dynamics model.
prediction_targets: Next-state/reward distributions and ensemble variance used as an error proxy.
training_horizon: Synthetic model rollouts augment offline policy learning under a penalized reward.
planning: Optimizes a policy in an uncertainty-penalized learned MDP.
uncertainty_safety: Subtracts a model-uncertainty penalty to approximate a lower bound on true return.
protocol_baselines: D4RL and related-task generalization against offline model-free and model-based baselines.
result_summary: The official paper reports stronger benchmark and related-task results, but reviews note that the practical Gaussian variance penalty is not identical to the theoretical error term.
limitation: Ensemble variance can be miscalibrated, and the continuous offline-RL setting differs from near-online CityFlow candidate scoring.
traffic_inspiration: Use lower-confidence candidate scores only if uncertainty is empirically calibrated against true CityFlow ranking error.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract and Sec. 4-5; official NeurIPS reviews/meta-review on variance penalty limitations

title: COMBO: Conservative Offline Model-Based Policy Optimization
motivation: Explicit neural-model uncertainty can be inaccurate and cause poor offline model-based RL performance.
state_action: Offline transitions plus model-generated out-of-support state-action tuples.
prediction_targets: A learned dynamics model supplies synthetic rollouts; a conservative Q function is regularized on out-of-support tuples.
training_horizon: Model rollouts generate training data for value learning rather than serving only as an MPC score.
planning: Policy optimization uses conservative values without requiring explicit uncertainty at decision time.
uncertainty_safety: Conservatism is imposed in the value function, avoiding reliance on a possibly unreliable uncertainty estimator.
protocol_baselines: Offline RL benchmarks, related unseen tasks, and image-based control against model-free and model-based baselines.
result_summary: The paper reports competitive or stronger results and a policy-improvement guarantee under its assumptions.
limitation: Adding a full offline conservative Q learner is a different project scope from the current planner and is not a minimal first change.
traffic_inspiration: Keep as a fallback if ensemble calibration fails; do not assume disagreement is automatically trustworthy.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract, Sec. 4-5 and Conclusion

title: MOReL: Model-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning
motivation: Provide a model-based offline RL framework whose learned surrogate discourages unknown state-action regions.
state_action: Offline continuous-control transitions; an uncertainty detector marks unfamiliar state-action inputs.
prediction_targets: Dynamics inside a pessimistic MDP plus an absorbing negative-reward state for unknown inputs.
training_horizon: Policy learning occurs in the pessimistic learned MDP.
planning: Any near-optimal policy solver can be used in the pessimistic MDP.
uncertainty_safety: Unknown state-action detection routes risky transitions to a strongly penalized absorbing state.
protocol_baselines: Standard offline RL benchmarks with theoretical lower-bound analysis and five-seed experiments noted by reviewers.
result_summary: The official paper reports matching or exceeding contemporary offline RL baselines under its benchmark protocol.
limitation: A binary unknown detector may be too coarse for traffic candidates that differ by one phase, and threshold sensitivity must be measured.
traffic_inspiration: A support gate is conceptually closer to MaxPressure fallback than unconstrained model search, but must be defined on trajectory data rather than invented heuristics.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract and Sec. 4-5; official NeurIPS reviews on unknown-state-action detector

title: Optimizing Traffic Control with Model-Based Learning: A Pessimistic Approach to Data-Efficient Policy Inference
motivation: Learn traffic-signal policies from cheaply collected cyclic-control data while managing offline distribution shift.
state_action: Traffic state vectors and discrete signal actions from an offline replay buffer.
prediction_targets: A finite empirical MDP: action-conditioned transition matrices and pessimistically shaped rewards over core states.
training_horizon: Value iteration solves the inferred MDP; nearest-neighbor transitions connect logged and evaluation states.
planning: Policy inference uses the solved finite MDP rather than neural multi-step candidate rollout.
uncertainty_safety: Distance from logged neighbors subtracts a fixed or adaptive cost from reward for OOD states/actions.
protocol_baselines: A signalized roundabout and a large multi-intersection SUMO environment; offline data are collected from cyclic signal control.
result_summary: The paper and repository describe data-efficient traffic control with pessimistic costs; exact table values are not reused here because the accessible supporting document protocol differs from our CityFlow setup.
limitation: The repository has no declared license, uses a non-neural finite MDP, and cannot be copied directly.
traffic_inspiration: The closest direct evidence for penalizing distance from traffic data support; compare its gate conceptually, not its implementation.
evidence_pointer: KDD paper Abstract; repo README; ADAC/dac_mdp.py:141-252,285-338,412-502

title: Boosting Efficiency in Task-Agnostic Exploration through Causal Knowledge
motivation: Collect data that improves task-agnostic world models more efficiently by learning and exploiting causal structure.
state_action: Factorized state variables plus action; the TSC case study is a single three-lane intersection with switch/stay action.
prediction_targets: One predictor per next-state factor, with inputs masked by a learned causal graph.
training_horizon: Online one-step world-model fitting and intrinsic exploration rewards based on prediction error/data usefulness.
planning: The world model guides exploration; it is not used as a multi-intersection deployment MPC controller.
uncertainty_safety: Prediction error becomes intrinsic reward; no ensemble, OOD lower bound, or fallback.
protocol_baselines: Synthetic systems, a single-intersection SUMO task, and MuJoCo tasks.
result_summary: The IJCAI page reports improved sample efficiency and reliability under its task-agnostic exploration setting.
limitation: Its TSC experiment has one intersection and binary switch/stay action; causal discovery and prediction error do not prove safe candidate ranking.
traffic_inspiration: Use known phase-movement topology as a supervised structural prior before attempting causal discovery.
evidence_pointer: paper Sec. 3-5 and official page; traffic/models/CausalWorldModel.py:9-79

title: Enhancing Traffic Signal Control through Model-Based Reinforcement Learning and Policy Reuse
motivation: Reduce retraining when traffic flows or road networks change.
state_action: Multi-intersection observations with adjacency; discrete actions enter a shared encoder-decoder and Q network.
prediction_targets: Action-conditioned next observation from a decoder; the encoder is shared with a Q network.
training_horizon: One-step transition prediction jointly learned with control; PRLight reuses source policies based on source-target similarity.
planning: Q-network control and policy reuse, not online MPC candidate ranking.
uncertainty_safety: Similarity-weighted policy selection; no calibrated ensemble or MaxPressure fallback.
protocol_baselines: Three road-network types and eight flow datasets; within-network flow transfer and cross-network transfer.
result_summary: The journal page reports faster adaptation and compares joint model-policy learning through ablation.
limitation: Repository lacks a declared license; the environmental model is used for transfer similarity, not demonstrated conservative planning.
traffic_inspiration: Reuse action-conditioned decoder and cross-flow protocol ideas; independently test whether similarity helps before heterogeneous pretraining.
evidence_pointer: journal Abstract/Introduction; PLight/EDQN.py:20-137 and repository data directories

title: ModelLight: Model-Based Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control
motivation: Adapt TSC policies to new traffic scenarios with fewer real simulator samples.
state_action: Single-intersection lane vehicle counts plus an explicit phase vector representing the selected discrete action.
prediction_targets: Next lane vehicle counts and reward using GP, ANN, or LSTM environment models.
training_horizon: One-step model fitting followed by recursively generated imaginary transitions for meta-RL updates.
planning: The model expands training data; execution uses a learned Q policy rather than online MPC.
uncertainty_safety: No ensemble disagreement, OOD support test, or rule-based fallback in the inspected core path.
protocol_baselines: Repository provides Hangzhou, Jinan, Atlanta, and Los Angeles scenarios and compares meta-RL/controller variants in the paper.
result_summary: Because this is an arXiv preprint, it is retained as direct TSC mechanism evidence but not treated as top-venue validation.
limitation: The action model is local and recursive synthetic data can compound error; the repository uses old TensorFlow/Keras components.
traffic_inspiration: It directly validates using a phase vector rather than an arbitrary action id, supporting phase-movement semantics.
evidence_pointer: paper Sec. 3-5; intersection_model.py:21-99,171-216 and metalearner.py:64-169

title: Image-Based Traffic Signal Control via World Models
venue: Frontiers of Information Technology & Electronic Engineering 23(12)
motivation: Use predictive traffic representations for proactive rather than purely reactive signal control.
state_action: Vehicle-position images and signal-control actions at an intersection.
prediction_targets: Latent/image traffic dynamics and multi-step imagined samples inspired by DreamerV2.
training_horizon: Multi-step imagined data train a controller; the controller acts directly at execution.
planning: World-model imagination supports policy optimization rather than executing video MPC online.
uncertainty_safety: No ensemble calibration or conservative fallback is established on the official page.
protocol_baselines: The article reports image prediction and TSC performance against common baselines; exact protocol is not comparable to our structured CityFlow state.
result_summary: The official abstract reports improved control and accurate image prediction in its setting.
limitation: Its image state, Dreamer-style controller, and likely compute/data requirements are outside the locked structured-state scope.
traffic_inspiration: Confirms that multi-step world-model imagination has been tried in TSC, so generic 'first World Model for traffic lights' is not a valid gap.
evidence_pointer: official article page lines 16-90 and full paper

title: X-Light: Cross-City Traffic Signal Control Using Transformer on Transformer as Meta Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learner
motivation: Transfer multi-agent TSC policies across cities rather than retraining each network from scratch.
state_action: Full MDP trajectories containing local and neighbor states, actions, and rewards.
prediction_targets: A lower transformer models intra-city neighborhood decision interactions; an upper transformer includes a dynamics prediction objective across scenarios.
training_horizon: Trajectory-level meta-training across multiple scenarios/cities.
planning: Learned actor/controller; not a learned environment used to score online candidates.
uncertainty_safety: No ensemble disagreement or MaxPressure fallback in the central method.
protocol_baselines: Multi-scenario training and zero-shot unseen-scenario evaluation against meta-RL and TSC baselines.
result_summary: The official IJCAI page reports +7.91% average zero-shot improvement and up to +16.3% in some cases under its protocol.
limitation: Its dynamics predictor is a representation/meta-learning auxiliary, not evidence that an MPC world model improves MaxPressure.
traffic_inspiration: Use full state-action-reward neighborhood trajectories for cross-city pretraining only after action-conditioned dynamics passes within-city tests.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract, Sec. 3-5, Fig. 4-7; official IJCAI page

title: CrossLight: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Cross-City Traffic Signal Control
motivation: Use source-city offline trajectories to initialize efficient online adaptation in a new city.
state_action: Traffic decision trajectories with traffic patterns and road-network structures across cities.
prediction_targets: Pattern-structure-aware trajectory representations and meta-knowledge rather than an explicit next-state MPC dynamics model.
training_horizon: Offline meta-training followed by online target-city adaptation.
planning: Policy optimization/adaptation, not candidate trajectory evaluation.
uncertainty_safety: No central dynamics ensemble or rule-based fallback.
protocol_baselines: Cross-city offline-to-online transfer against cross-city and offline/online RL baselines.
result_summary: Formal KDD publication establishes a recent cross-city comparison point; its metrics must not be merged with single-flow CityFlow results.
limitation: Cross-city gains may come from representation and online adaptation, not world-model prediction.
traffic_inspiration: A future heterogeneous pretraining claim must compare against CrossLight/X-Light rather than only single-city controllers.
evidence_pointer: paper Abstract and Sec. 3-5; KDD DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671927

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control through Universal Communication Method
motivation: Communicate information that is important to neighboring intersections rather than sharing observations heuristically.
state_action: Lane flow, green/phase features, road relations, and local discrete phase actions.
prediction_targets: Predict phase impact and outgoing road volumes that become neighbor inputs.
training_horizon: Auxiliary one-step phase/volume prediction losses are trained with DQN control.
planning: DQN chooses phases; predictions form communication features rather than a candidate MPC score.
uncertainty_safety: No ensemble or conservative fallback.
protocol_baselines: CityFlow Jinan, Hangzhou, New York, and two Shanghai datasets; the repository warns its CityFlow travel-time definition differs from upstream.
result_summary: The official IJCAI page reports universal gains when UniComm is added to existing methods and stronger UniLight performance.
limitation: Repository metric semantics differ from upstream CityFlow and outputs are not conditioned on all neighbors' simultaneous selected actions.
traffic_inspiration: Predict movement-level outgoing volumes and route them along road relations; preserve our simulator's metric contract.
evidence_pointer: official IJCAI page; rl/models/innerModels/NewModel.py:8-78 and rl/agents/NewModelAgent.py:61-153

title: MaCAR: Urban Traffic Light Control via Active Multi-Agent Communication and Action Rectification
motivation: Independent synchronous intersection actions can conflict and bias local action values.
state_action: Multi-intersection observations and synchronous joint traffic-light actions.
prediction_targets: Traffic after agents' synchronous actions and corresponding action values.
training_horizon: Traffic forecasting and action-value rectification are coupled to multi-agent RL training.
planning: Predictions rectify future actions instead of running a standalone world-model MPC.
uncertainty_safety: No explicit epistemic uncertainty or fallback.
protocol_baselines: Synthetic and real-world TSC datasets against contemporary multi-agent TSC baselines.
result_summary: The official IJCAI page reports improvement over state-of-the-art methods in its protocol.
limitation: The method corrects learned action values; it does not isolate multi-step model ranking versus MaxPressure.
traffic_inspiration: Strongest direct precedent for explicitly conditioning traffic predictions on synchronous neighboring actions.
evidence_pointer: official IJCAI page Abstract; paper Sec. 3-5

title: GPLight: Grouped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Traffic Signal Control
motivation: Balance per-intersection heterogeneity against parameter and optimization cost in large networks.
state_action: Real-time flow and fine-grained road topology define dynamically learned intersection groups.
prediction_targets: Group assignments and group-shared value/control representations, not environment transitions.
training_horizon: End-to-end MARL with mutual-information and group-separation objectives.
planning: QMIX-style grouped policy learning.
uncertainty_safety: No world-model uncertainty or fallback.
protocol_baselines: Synthetic and real networks up to 1,089 intersections; baselines include FixedTime, MaxPressure, IntelliLight, CoLight, and MPLight.
result_summary: Table 3 reports 735.51 s on Grid33x33-Bi versus 2171.13 for MaxPressure, but this large-network protocol is not directly comparable to our Jinan run.
limitation: The gain is a controller/grouping result, not evidence for learned dynamics; scale and metric definitions must be replicated before numeric comparison.
traffic_inspiration: Use as a strong large-network RL boundary and as evidence that static parameter sharing may miss intersection heterogeneity.
evidence_pointer: paper Sec. 5, Fig. 7, Tables 3-4; official IJCAI page

title: PressLight: Learning Max Pressure Control to Coordinate Traffic Signals in Arterial Network
motivation: Tie RL state/reward design to max-pressure traffic theory rather than ad-hoc reward engineering.
state_action: Lane pressure/queue information and discrete signal phases.
prediction_targets: Action values and cumulative pressure-based reward; no environment transition model.
training_horizon: Model-free value learning over simulator interactions.
planning: Greedy phase selection from learned Q values.
uncertainty_safety: No learned-model uncertainty; pressure semantics provide the domain prior.
protocol_baselines: Arterial and network traffic scenarios against transportation and RL baselines.
result_summary: LibSignal later finds PressLight among the most stable/sample-efficient agents under unified comparisons, reinforcing its baseline role.
limitation: It does not test a world model, but omitting it would make a new TSC method comparison incomplete.
traffic_inspiration: Preserve pressure/movement semantics in the model and include PressLight or an equivalent pressure-RL implementation as a strong learned baseline.
evidence_pointer: KDD paper Sec. 3-5; LibSignal Appendix A.6.1-A.6.4

title: CoLight: Learning Network-Level Cooperation for Traffic Signal Control
motivation: Learn network-level coordination by selecting influential neighboring intersections.
state_action: Per-intersection traffic features, graph neighbors, and discrete phases.
prediction_targets: Graph-attention features and Q values, not next traffic state.
training_horizon: Model-free multi-agent value learning.
planning: Learned per-intersection decisions with graph attention.
uncertainty_safety: No world-model uncertainty or fallback.
protocol_baselines: Multiple synthetic and real traffic networks; reimplemented in LibSignal for cross-simulator comparison.
result_summary: Formal publication and unified reimplementation make it a graph-coordination baseline, not a source of world-model claims.
limitation: State communication alone cannot tell whether neighbors' selected actions causally change a candidate rollout.
traffic_inspiration: Compare action-semantic world models against graph-attention controllers to separate prediction gains from generic graph modeling gains.
evidence_pointer: CIKM paper Sec. 3-5; LibSignal model/benchmark discussion

title: GMAN: A Graph Multi-Attention Network for Traffic Prediction
motivation: Reduce long-horizon traffic forecasting error caused by complex spatial and temporal dependence.
state_action: Historical sensor traffic features on a road-network graph; no signal-control action.
prediction_targets: A direct future sequence of traffic volume or speed using encoder-decoder attention.
training_horizon: Direct multi-step sequence prediction with transform attention from history to future slots.
planning: No controller or action-conditioned planning.
uncertainty_safety: Deterministic predictions; no model-based control safety layer.
protocol_baselines: Two real-world traffic volume/speed datasets; reports up to 4% MAE improvement at one hour.
result_summary: The direct future decoder is evidence against assuming recursive one-step rollout is the only multi-step design.
limitation: Without signal actions, it cannot rank counterfactual phase plans and must not be presented as a World Model controller baseline.
traffic_inspiration: Test direct 1-5-step prediction as an alternative to recursive rollout, while injecting actions at every future step.
evidence_pointer: official AAAI page Abstract; paper Fig. 1 and Sec. 3-4

title: STDEN: Towards Physics-Guided Neural Networks for Traffic Flow Prediction
motivation: Combine data-driven traffic prediction with a physically interpretable traffic-flow mechanism.
state_action: Historical traffic flows on a road graph; no signal action.
prediction_targets: Future flow generated through a latent potential-energy differential equation network.
training_horizon: Spatio-temporal flow prediction trained on real Beijing traffic datasets.
planning: No control or candidate evaluation.
uncertainty_safety: Physics prior supports interpretation but does not quantify epistemic uncertainty.
protocol_baselines: Three Beijing datasets against traffic forecasting baselines plus a physical-meaning case study.
result_summary: The official AAAI page reports stronger forecasting and an interpretable case study.
limitation: The latent potential formulation is not directly linked to CityFlow movement conservation under changing phases.
traffic_inspiration: Prefer explicit movement inflow/outflow conservation as the smallest traffic prior; only add differential equations if that simpler prior fails.
evidence_pointer: official AAAI page Abstract; paper Sec. 3-5

title: UniST: A Prompt-Empowered Universal Model for Urban Spatio-Temporal Prediction
motivation: Learn a universal urban spatio-temporal predictor across cities, domains, and data-scarce scenarios.
state_action: Grid or graph spatio-temporal observations across more than 20 scenarios; no control action.
prediction_targets: Future spatio-temporal fields through masked pretraining and knowledge-guided prompt tuning.
training_horizon: Large-scale pretraining followed by scenario-specific prompt tuning, including few-shot and zero-shot protocols.
planning: No TSC controller or action-conditioned MPC.
uncertainty_safety: No conservative control gate.
protocol_baselines: More than 20 urban spatio-temporal scenarios with full-data, few-shot, and zero-shot prediction comparisons.
result_summary: Formal KDD evidence supports heterogeneous pretraining for prediction, not automatically for control.
limitation: Repository declares no license and its input/output formats do not represent phase-conditioned counterfactual dynamics.
traffic_inspiration: Use schema masks and shared pretraining only after adding action/movement tokens and evaluating control ranking, not just forecast MAE.
evidence_pointer: KDD paper Abstract and Sec. 3-5; repository README pretraining/prompt-tuning protocol

title: Libsignal: An Open Library for Traffic Signal Control
motivation: Make TSC comparisons fair across algorithms, datasets, and CityFlow/SUMO simulators.
state_action: Unified World/Intersection/Generator interfaces expose lane counts, waiting, pressure, phase, and heterogeneous action spaces.
prediction_targets: Benchmark infrastructure, not a learned environment model.
training_horizon: Unified training/evaluation interfaces with cross-simulator calibration and recorded hyperparameters.
planning: Supports multiple fixed, heuristic, value-based, and policy-gradient agents.
uncertainty_safety: Not applicable; its value is evaluation semantics and reproducibility.
protocol_baselines: CityFlow and SUMO, nine calibrated datasets, model reimplementations, standard deviations, and convergence comparisons.
result_summary: The appendix reports PressLight and IDQN as stable/sample-efficient in many settings and warns actor-critic methods can be much harder to converge on large networks.
limitation: A library benchmark does not remove differences in phase definitions, flow files, reward, or simulator forks; each comparison contract still needs validation.
traffic_inspiration: Adopt its baseline/evaluation discipline and preserve exact metric semantics; do not copy GPL code into an MIT project.
evidence_pointer: official journal lines 38-40,122-128,245-326; Appendix A.2-A.8

title: Diagnosing Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control
motivation: Question whether complicated RL states and ad-hoc rewards actually optimize travel time.
state_action: Concise traffic state and pressure-related reward grounded in classical traffic theory.
prediction_targets: Model-free action values; no learned transition model.
training_horizon: RL training evaluated on synthetic and real traffic datasets.
planning: Learned traffic-light policy.
uncertainty_safety: No world-model uncertainty; the risk lesson is representation/reward mismatch.
protocol_baselines: Synthetic and real TSC datasets against contemporary methods, with targeted state/reward analysis.
result_summary: The paper argues that simpler theory-grounded state/reward design can outperform more complex choices.
limitation: It is a preprint and does not test multi-step learned dynamics, but it is an important falsifier of complexity-for-complexity's-sake.
traffic_inspiration: Any World Model gain must survive a strong pressure representation and cannot be attributed only to a larger network.
evidence_pointer: arXiv Abstract and Sec. 3-5
